# Engine inventory: goodvibes-sdk to packages/engine

Every source file of goodvibes-sdk (`packages/*/src`, tests excluded) with its disposition, grouped by the intent's engine subsystems. Nothing is dropped unless it is specific to WRFC or QEMU; everything else uses Jev where judgment applies or is ported exactly. Jev is in place of WRFC: WRFC code is JEV in the contract runner, and docs/inventory/wrfc-to-jev.md maps each WRFC function to its Jev form. A JEV file lists each place it decides something by guesswork today and the battery or pattern from `packages/judgment` that replaces it. A PORT file with decision points keeps its code but its guesswork moves to the JEV subsystem the intent names (for providers, the new routing subsystem). HOIST applies to product modules moving into the engine and is recorded in the product inventories.

Files: 2373. PORT 2082, JEV 289, DROP 2. Decision points: 646.

### Decision points

| Where | Guessed today | Replaced by |
|---|---|---|
| `sdk/src/platform/integrations/delivery.ts:171` | classifyDeliveryError() used to parse an HTTP status out of the message text (`/http\s+(\d{3})/`), lower-case the message and check it for 'timeout'/'aborted'/'econnrefused'/'enotfound'/'network' to call the failure retryable, call any other TypeError terminal, and default the rest to retryable | done (E.9): readFailureTransience (line 164; `classifyDeliveryError` line 175 delegates to it). Structured facts first (DeliveryError class, Retry-After, `status`/`statusCode` field, errno code on the error or its cause, timeout error class), then one `engine.failure-reading` reading (`readFailure`, line 171) composed in code (billing permanent; transient network retried; category table; unsettled retried within the attempt budget). Senders now throw `HttpStatusError` with the status as a field. Live proof: `bun run --cwd packages/engine delivery:proof` |
| `sdk/src/platform/automation/delivery-manager.ts:244` | the retry-or-give-up call in deliverText took classifyDeliveryError's keyword verdict to choose between another attempt after the policy's cooldown, `failed`, and `dead_lettered` | done (E.9): readFailureTransience, the same decision as the integration queue |
| `sdk/src/platform/automation/manager-runtime-delivery.ts:106` | scheduleAutomationFailureFollowUp re-ran every failed run under a retry policy, with no view of whether the failure could clear | done (E.9): the retry happens only when readAutomationRunTransience (line 57) finds the failure transient (or the run was cancelled, which has no failure to read) |
| `sdk/src/platform/automation/manager-runtime-execution.ts:237` | a run that failed to start was reported `retryable: true` on AUTOMATION_RUN_FAILED whatever the error | done (E.9): `retryable` from readAutomationRunTransience over the thrown error |
| `sdk/src/platform/automation/manager-runtime-reconcile.ts:174` | a failed or lost agent run was reported `retryable: false` on AUTOMATION_RUN_FAILED whatever the agent's error said | done (E.9): the agent's error text is read (settleAutomationRunFailure through readAutomationRunTransience) before the event and the follow-up; a lost agent state (line 99) is retryable by structure |
| `sdk/src/platform/automation/manager-runtime.ts:535` | a remote runner's failed result was reported `retryable: false` on AUTOMATION_RUN_FAILED whatever its error said | done (E.9): the reported error text is read (readAutomationRunTransience) before the event and the follow-up |

### Decision points

| Where | Guessed today | Replaced by |
|---|---|---|
| `sdk/src/platform/daemon/auto-updater.ts:283` | Whether self-update has stopped working and the owner must be told: guessed from a count of consecutive thrown update checks reaching alertAfterFailedChecks (default 3, config update.alertAfterFailedChecks), standing in for "persistent, not a transient network blip" | Failure-transience reading of the check error text (readFailureTransience pattern, choice transient or persistent): "Will this update-check failure clear on its own on the next attempt, or does it need someone to act?" A persistent reading alerts the owner (still rate limited by the 12h quiet window, code); the count cutoff is removed |
| `sdk/src/platform/daemon/surface-actions.ts:248` | parseSurfaceControlCommand matches the trimmed inbound channel text against `^(status\|cancel\|retry)\s+([a-z0-9:_-]+)` to decide whether the message is a control command for a run, agent or session or a message for the assistant; on a match nine adapters answer with the command result and never submit the message, so ordinary sentences that start with those words are swallowed | a choice pattern: is this message asking to show the status of, cancel, or retry a run, agent or session (and which id), or is it a message for the assistant? The named id's existence stays a code lookup |
| `sdk/src/platform/daemon/surface-card-gate.ts:77` | refuseCardShapedIngress refuses the message when detectCardShapes (security/card-shapes.ts) finds a Luhn-valid 13-19 digit run, or, with a card keyword (cvv, cvc, card, expiry, security code) anywhere in the text, any bare 3-4 digit run or MM/YY pair | a yes/no pattern: does this message contain a payment card number, security code or expiry date? (see Notes on sending the text to Jev) |
| `sdk/src/platform/daemon/surface-conversation-gate.ts:107` | gateSurfaceSpawn calls classifyInboundIntent(inboundText) (agents/conversation-gate.ts:275) on the owner's inbound text; it strips REQUEST_PREAMBLES regexes, tests the clause head against a WORK_VERBS set, skips QUESTION_OPENERS, and also calls a message work when a CODE_REFERENCE regex and any work verb appear; needsAgreement and the whole propose-vs-spawn branch turn on that result | the intake intent battery named at agents/conversation-gate.ts:214 (choice: converse or propose work): is this inbound message a request to do work, or conversation? |
| `sdk/src/platform/daemon/work-proposal-reply.ts:82` | tryResolveWorkProposalReplyFromChannel calls parseWorkProposalReply (agents/conversation-gate.ts:453), which reads the reply as affirmative or negative by the UNAMBIGUOUS_AFFIRMATIVE, STANDALONE_AFFIRMATIVE, UNAMBIGUOUS_NEGATIVE and STANDALONE_NEGATIVE regexes and splits a trailing steering note with NOTE_CONJUNCTIONS; accept starts the work, decline drops it | a reply pattern: read the owner's message against the pending proposal's summary as approve, reject, amend or unclear, carrying any trailing text as steering on the resolution |

### Decision points

| Where | Guessed today | Replaced by |
|---|---|---|
| `sdk/src/platform/git/service.ts:9` | isMissingGitIdentityError() (L11-15) matches a commit failure's lowercased message against three git wordings ('author identity unknown', 'please tell me who you are', 'unable to auto-detect email address') to decide whether to retry the commit with a fallback identity (L302) | Jev yes/no: "Does this commit failure say git has no author name or email configured?", in place of the three-phrase list |
| `sdk/src/platform/git/service.ts:373` | merge() decides a failure with no structured conflict entries was a merge conflict (return conflicts) rather than another error (rethrow) by message.includes('CONFLICT') | Jev yes/no: "Does this merge failure report a merge conflict?" |
| `sdk/src/platform/git/service.ts:52` | conflictPathsFromMergeOutput() (L52, L56) takes a `CONFLICT (...)` line's text after the first colon, minus 'Merge conflict in', as the conflicted file, which yields prose for modify/delete and rename conflicts | Jev candidate selection: "Which of these spans of the merge failure text name a file that conflicted?" |
| `sdk/src/platform/intelligence/import-graph.ts:34` | SKIP_DIRS (applied at L172) skips directories named 'dist', '.next', '.nuxt', '.cache', '__pycache__' as not project source, by name | Jev yes/no per directory: "Is this directory build output, a cache or generated content rather than the project's own source?" |

Built new for this subsystem in E.12 (new files, not goodvibes-sdk sources, so not rows above): `sdk/src/platform/observe/` reads the state layer's decision log (`<workspace>/.goodvibes/<surface>/decisions.sqlite`) for accuracy against confidence where fixtures, owner corrections or outcomes left ground truth (a `truth` note, decision log schema 3), threshold sweeps over logged readings with no new calls, drift per window with the change flag computed in code (outcome mix, mean signal, answering model), question discovery (readings stuck in confirm or escalate by decision, site and question), calls outside a registered battery, judgment cost (Jev calls priced through runtime/cost/attribution.ts `priceRecord`, unpriced for an unknown model), and the `judgment-accuracy` eval suite; every threshold is in `observe/thresholds.ts`. It also holds the TUI hoists: `observe/eval-registry.ts` (goodvibes-tui `src/panels/eval-registry.ts`, ported exactly) and `observe/cost-tracker.ts` (the session and agent cost tracking state goodvibes-tui kept inside `src/panels/cost-tracker-panel.ts`); neither has a decision point, since both are bookkeeping and token arithmetic. `scripts/observe-report.ts` (`bun run observe:report`) prints every analysis for a log, `scripts/observe-proof.ts` (`bun run observe:proof`) seeds a log from a live calibration run and shows each analysis producing output, and `scripts/judgment-lint.ts` (`bun run judgment:lint`, in validate) fails when a registered decision has no fixture for one of its answers or engine source asks Jev outside a registered decision.

### Decision points

| Where | Guessed today | Replaced by |
|---|---|---|
| `sdk/src/platform/payments/cart.ts:118` | RECURRING_PATTERNS, a fixed list of regexes over the merchant's order-summary text (subscri.., recurring, auto-renew, per month/year, free trial, save card for future) matched in detectRecurringCharge to decide if a checkout enrolls a recurring charge | battery yes/no (noul) question: "does this order summary describe a recurring or subscription charge?", banded so any non-confident or positive answer refuses the purchase (conservative-by-design, matching today's refuse-on-any-match behavior) |
| `sdk/src/platform/payments/merchant-judge-model.ts:61` | RESPONSE_INSTRUCTIONS, a hand-written prompt asking the model for a JSON object {qualifies, confident, recourse, marketplace}, plus parseVerdict (line 87) parsing that free-text/JSON answer into a typed verdict, in createModelMerchantJudge (line 134) | choice-over-options reading ("does this registrable domain qualify as an established retailer with real recourse: yes / no / not confident") plus a short choice reading for marketplace kind (none / buyer-protection / per-seller), banded so not-confident and no both resolve to not-qualifying, matching the intent's merchant-qualification and recourse-category batteries |
| `sdk/src/platform/payments/notice-delivery.ts:118` | APPROVAL_WORDS and VETO_WORDS, two hand-written keyword maps (approve/approved/yes/y/ok/okay/go/buy it -> approve; deny/denied/no/n/cancel/stop/don't -> deny; and the mirrored veto map where go/ok/yes/approve acknowledge and stop/no/cancel/wait/don't/hold object), read in parsePaymentReply (line 141) by exact or first-word match | the judgment package's reply pattern (read a human reply: approve, reject, amend, unclear) run twice, once for the approval-window vocabulary (approve/deny) and once for the veto-window vocabulary (acknowledge/object), so the same words can be read oppositely on the two windows exactly as today, with an unclear reading falling through to the window's own silence rule |
| `sdk/src/platform/payments/order-correlation.ts:176` | ORDER_NUMBER, SHIP_DATE and TRACKING, three regexes over the confirmation email body text, run in extractConfirmationFacts (line 187) to pull out an order number, a ship date and a tracking reference | the judgment package's structure-recovery pattern (extract named structured fields, order number / ship date / tracking reference, from free text, with a null field when none is found) in place of the three regexes; the domain and time-window correlation logic itself stays deterministic |
| `sdk/src/platform/payments/cart.ts:62` | assertCartMatchesRequest takes a cart line as the requested item when its label, lowercased with punctuation removed, equals the owner's requested label | entity alignment between the merchant's cart labels and the owner's requested items; quantities stay compared in code (recorded, owned by E.10) |
| `sdk/src/platform/payments/entry-surface.ts:137` | scanForCardDetails reads a 13 to 19 digit run, an MM/YY-shaped date, or (when a code was asked for) a bare three or four digits as card details sent over a remote channel | yes/no over the message: does it carry payment card details (recorded, owned by E.10) |
| `sdk/src/platform/payments/order-correlation.ts:131` | a mail from a purchase's registrable domain within six hours of it counts as that purchase's confirmation | yes/no over the mail and each same-domain candidate: is this the confirmation of this order (recorded, owned by E.10) |
| `sdk/src/platform/payments/shipping.ts:48` | rankShippingOptions calls the cheapest delivery option normal, the next fast and the next fastest | candidate selection of the option for each tier over the options' labels and costs (recorded, owned by E.10) |
| `sdk/src/platform/payments/taint-gate.ts:169` | the purchase item and stated limit are refused as derived from untrusted text when they share 8 words or a 40-character span with it | yes/no per untrusted source: is this value derived from this text (the content-taint reading; recorded, owned by E.10) |

The routing subsystem these points moved to is new engine code in `packages/engine/sdk/src/platform/routing/` (exported as `@goodvibes-jev/engine/sdk/platform/routing`): the request batteries and tier policy, the route planner (`createRoutePlanner`), model tiers, model identity, catalog provider access, the provider protocol readings, the hoisted task route planner and route tool (`task-routes/`, from goodvibes-agent) and the hoisted user error line (`user-error.ts`, from goodvibes-tui). Every decision is registered in `routing/judgment-registry.ts` for calibration.

| `sdk/src/platform/state/knowledge-injection.ts:180` | Formerly: scoreKnowledge added confidence, 40/20/-30 for reviewed/fresh/stale, 20 per task token and 15 per scope token found as substrings, plus semantic similarity times 70. | Implemented: `engine.state.knowledge-relevance` item `relevant`, one request per shortlisted record; no drops the record; the result is ordered by probability, ties by updatedAt. |
| `sdk/src/platform/state/knowledge-injection.ts:127` | Formerly: determineReason explained an injection by substring tests of task and scope tokens, else a similarity percentage or a fixed phrase. | Implemented: items `task_match` and `scope_match` of the same battery, in the same request, name the evidence; the similarity percentage is the vector index's own number. |
| `sdk/src/platform/state/knowledge-injection.ts:141` | Formerly: determineIngestMode labelled hybrid, semantic or keyword from hasKeywordMatch's substring yes/no plus whether a similarity was present. | Implemented: `task_match` or `scope_match` read yes, composed in code with whether the vector index shortlisted the record. |
| `sdk/src/platform/state/memory-consolidation.ts:199` | Formerly: normalizeKey (lowercase, strip punctuation) and exact equality of two records' details told a duplicate from a contradiction. | Implemented: `engine.state.memory-alignment` (entity alignment, medium band; distinct ends the pair) then `engine.state.memory-agreement` (restates, conflicts; low band); code acts only on an act outcome, and a conflict wins over a restatement. |
| `sdk/src/platform/state/memory-consolidation.ts:263` | supersedes: in a same-scope contradiction the newer record (updatedAt) wins and the older is marked stale when the newer is at least as reviewed, deciding from timestamps which statement is correct. | New: choice item `replaces` (a_replaces_b, b_replaces_a, neither) on `engine.state.memory-agreement`, asked in the same request, acted on only for a conflict; medium band. | `sdk/src/platform/state/memory-store.ts:330` (memory-search-ranking.ts:35) | Formerly: scoreRecord (memory-store-helpers.ts) added confidence, +30 query substring of summary, +20 of detail, +15 semantic, up to 25 for tags, -20 flagged. | Implemented: `engine.state.memory-search` rerank over the SQL matches (rerankRetrieved), low band. |
